plan.rationale: Frozen objective is latency_ms of one complete offline batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward bounded by torch.cuda.synchronize() on both sides (resnet_inference.py:42-47), single device, no distributed backend. The torch collector already ran and attribution is complete (coverage.json: 60/60 CUDA kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 autograd ranges), so kernel-to-operator attribution, overlap and CUDA-graph tracing questions are already resolved and nsys adds nothing. The remaining open question for reducing synchronized wall latency is the host/device split inside the timed window: whether wall time is dominated by GPU execution intervals or by CPU submission and Python dispatch gaps between the ~60 kernels. execution_timeline is selected for its separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events and per-device intervals (clock alignment bounds apply to CPU submissions only; GPU readiness may remain unknown). python_runtime is selected for a warmed cProfile call trace of the same forward path (transformers 5.16.1 module dispatch) to attribute host dispatch and binding cost; it perturbs execution, so its inclusive/self times are used only for attribution, never as performance scores or GPU compute durations. Communication-family collectors (nccl_tuning, collective_calibration) are excluded because the task is single-device with communication not_applicable. device_telemetry is excluded because its device-wide NVML PCIe/utilization/memory readings cannot be attributed to the ms-scale timed unit, which contains no host transfer (GPU-resident input). binding_cost and candidate_diagnostics are excluded because no candidate exists yet. nsys is not requested: attribution is already complete and there is no multi-stream/overlap or graph-tracing question in this single-device inference workload. No PCIe/NVLink traffic is inferred from logical payload sizes. Unavailable dimensions are listed with observed reasons.
